name: Fontainebleau Miami Beach
positioning: Large Miami Beach resort on Millionaire's Row whose design essentially launched the so-called Miami-Modern style
best_for: Travelers who want a resort they could easily stay at without leaving the grounds
Fans of Miami Beach history, from the Rat Pack to Goldfinger
Spa-goers who want a hydrotherapy circuit, mineral pools and a steam room

facts.text: The resort is on Millionaire's Row, almost its own neighborhood, and is within reach of South Beach.
The resort's main tower is curved.
The Rat Pack spent enough time at the hotel to make it the it-place to be.
Guest rooms and suites offer sweeping ocean and city views.
Rooms in the Versailles, Sorrento and Tresor towers are pretty quiet, while the Chateau tower has more of a party vibe.
Room types include an Oceanfront Guestroom with Balcony.
Specialty suites include the La Baie Presidential Suite.
Besides the Bowtie Pool, guests have access to other pools, including the Oasis Pool, with cabanas and loungers.
Lapis Spa offers Lapis Water Journeys, a mineral-enriched hydrotherapy service.
The events calendar includes morning yoga on the beach and circuit classes on Ocean Lawn.
Bleau Bar is the venue once graced by Frank Sinatra.
The resort is home to LIV nightclub.

highlights.text: The hotel's design essentially launched the so-called Miami-Modern style.
The hotel has been the background to several movies and TV shows, notably the James Bond movie Goldfinger.
A huge, freeform pool spreads out among the gardens.
Lapis Spa has a co-ed hydrotherapy circuit, restorative mineral pools and a eucalyptus-infused steam room.
The Bleau Paradise Ritual for Two takes place in a private oceanfront spa suite, with an aromatherapy hydro soak for two.

considerations.text: With the sheer volume of rooms, things get busy; guests range from conference delegates to families to party crowds.
Wi-Fi is included in the resort fee.
Lapis Spa guests must be 18 or older, and access to the spa facilities requires purchasing a spa service or package.
